subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Losses Loom Larger Than Gains
description: A quick win: understand Losses Loom Larger Than Gains.

hook.text: Would you accept a coin flip: heads you win $150, tails you lose $100? Most people refuse. The gain isn't big enough.

buildup.text: Loss aversion means losses hurt roughly twice as much as equivalent gains feel good. The ratio is about 2:1.

discovery.text: This asymmetry is hardwired. Brain scans show losses activate the amygdala more intensely than gains.

twist.text: Loss aversion declines for tiny amounts. Most people will flip a coin for $1. The pain threshold matters.

climax.text: Understanding the 2:1 ratio means framing gains as twice the size of potential losses to get a yes.

punchline.text: To sell a risk, make the gain twice the loss.

quiz.question: What is the approximate loss aversion ratio?
options: Losses hurt 5 times more than gains
Losses hurt about twice as much as gains
Gains and losses feel equally intense
